- What is the deletion workflow when we request erasure (API/console/support)? Timeline and proof?

Hi Marco — thanks for the doc and for flagging the deadline. Below are concise, copy-ready responses you can drop into the questionnaire (I kept language explicit; happy to tweak for procurement/legal tone).

1) Where data lives (region)
- Hosted API tenant data is stored in the cloud region selected at account creation. For Cedar, your default region is us-west-2. Processing may briefly span service components in the same geographic region for routing and autoscaling; we do not proactively replicate tenant request/response data to other geographic regions unless configured as part of an authorized failover policy or a dedicated cross-region backup (requires customer opt-in).

2) Default retention windows
- Request/response bodies and associated request metadata (headers, tokens, traces) are retained by default for 30 days for operational debugging and fraud detection.
- Aggregated telemetry (metrics, BPF-style sampling) is retained for 13 months for platform analytics.

3) Replication & backups
- Regular system backups (service configuration and infrastructure state) are taken daily and retained for 90 days. These backups are encrypted at rest with customer-independent KMS keys by default and are stored within the same region as the tenant.
- Cross-region replication of request/response data does not occur unless explicitly enabled in an enterprise contract for disaster recovery.

4) Deletion / erasure workflow
- Customers may initiate data deletion via: 1) the Console (Account > Data > Request Erasure), 2) the Delete API endpoint (POST /v1/customers/{id}/erase), or 3) by submitting a verified support request.
- Once a deletion request is submitted, active data is removed within 72 hours. Background purge of cached/queued copies and log derivatives completes within 30 days. We will provide a deletion certificate (timestamped) on completion.

5) Backups & keys
- Backups are encrypted using AES-256. For customers requiring dedicated key control, we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) under a Private deployment or as part of an enterprise-keying add-on.

Notes / tradeoffs
- If your security policy requires sub-30-day retention for request contents, we can propose a retention contract and technical configuration that truncates stored payloads sooner or routes requests to a Dedicated/Private deployment.

I'll attach a spreadsheet with the short answers formatted for your questionnaire (see attachment). Let me know if you want these responses reworded for legal review.

Quick summary (one-liners you can paste into procurement):

- Deletion: request via Console/API/support; active purge within 72 hours, full backend purge within 30 days; deletion certificate provided.
- Backups: daily encrypted snapshots retained 90 days; customer-managed KMS supported for enterprise/private deployments.
